entry: Large [[Tarantula|tarantula]] of northern South America (*Theraphosa blondi*). It is the largest [[Spider|spider]] in the world by mass, weighing up to 175 g, and by body length, up to 13 cm. Despite its name, it rarely preys on birds; its diet is mainly other large [[Arthropod|arthropods]], worms and [[Amphibian|amphibians]], and it also takes [[Rodent|rodents]], lizards and [[Snake|snakes]]. Threatened individuals release urticating hairs that irritate skin and mucous membranes. Its [[Venom|venom]] is relatively harmless, with effects comparable to a [[Wasp|wasp]] sting.

City, Amhara Region, northern Ethiopia (pop., 2021: 443,156). Gondar lies north of Lake Tana and was the capital of the [[Ethiopian Empire]] and of the later Begemder Province. Emperor Fasilides chose it as his royal camp in 1636, and it became a trading center where caravans from [[Sudan]] and the [[Red Sea]] converged. Fasilides built the Fasil Ghebbi, or Fasilides Castle, and five other churches in the capital. The remains of several royal castles, including the Fasil Ghebbi, form a [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]], and the city has been called the "Camelot of Africa." The name Gondar first appears during the reign of [[Amda Seyon I]], for a regiment of soldiers.

Ancient paleocontinent assembled in the Neoproterozoic. Its remnants make up about two-thirds of today's continental area, including [[South America]], Africa, [[Antarctica]], Australia, Zealandia, Arabia and the Indian subcontinent. In the Paleozoic it was the largest continental crust, covering some 100,000,000 sq km (39,000,000 sq mi). It fused with Laurasia during the [[Carboniferous]] to form [[Pangaea]]. Fragmentation began in the Early [[Jurassic]], around 180 million years ago, and the Antarctic land bridge broke during the [[Paleogene]], separating Antarctica from South America and Australia.

1939 American epic historical romance film directed by Victor Fleming. Adapted from Margaret Mitchell's 1936 novel, it was produced by David O. Selznick and follows Scarlett O'Hara, played by [[Vivien Leigh]], through the [[American Civil War]] and [[Reconstruction era|Reconstruction]]. Released on December 15, 1939, it won 10 [[Academy Awards]] from 13 nominations, including Best Picture, and Hattie McDaniel became the first African American to win an Academy Award. It was the highest-earning film up to its time and, adjusted for inflation, remains the highest-grossing film in history. Critics have called it historical negationism that glorifies slavery and the [[Lost Cause of the Confederacy|Lost Cause]] myth, while others credit it with changing how African Americans were depicted on screen. It was one of 25 inaugural films selected for the National Film Registry in 1989.

[[Dwarf planet]] in the scattered disc beyond [[Neptune]]. Discovered in July 2007 by Megan Schwamb, Michael Brown and David Rabinowitz at Palomar Observatory, it was announced in January 2009. At about 1,230 km (760 mi) in diameter, it is similar in size to Pluto's moon [[Charon (moon)|Charon]] and may be in [[Hydrostatic equilibrium|hydrostatic equilibrium]]. Its name, from a Chinese water god, was chosen through an online poll in 2019. Its surface is very red, likely from [[Organic compound|organic compounds]] called tholins. Its slow rotation may have been caused by tidal forces from its [[Natural satellite|satellite]], Xiangliu.

[[Sexually transmitted infection]] caused by the bacterium *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*, also called the clap. It spreads through sexual contact and from mother to child during birth, and many infected people have no symptoms. In men it can cause pain on urination and penile discharge; in women, vaginal discharge or pelvic pain. Untreated infection in women can cause pelvic inflammatory disease, which can scar the fallopian tubes and lead to later [[Ectopic pregnancy|ectopic pregnancy]]. Gonorrhea is also associated with an increased risk of [[Prostate cancer|prostate cancer]]. Treatment is usually an injection of ceftriaxone with oral [[Azithromycin|azithromycin]], though resistance to many earlier [[Antibiotic|antibiotics]] has developed. [[Condom|Condoms]], limiting sex to one uninfected partner, and abstinence prevent infection. An estimated 33 to 106 million new cases occur each year, and in 2015 the disease caused about 700 deaths.

Pair of agreements signed on April 10, 1998, also called the Belfast Agreement. It ended most of the violence of the [[The Troubles|Troubles]], the conflict in [[Northern Ireland]] since the late 1960s. It combines a multi-party agreement among most of Northern Ireland's political parties with a British–Irish agreement between the governments of the [[United Kingdom]] and [[Ireland]]. It restored self-government to Northern Ireland through power sharing and created North–South and East–West institutions. Voters across the island approved it in [[Referendum|referendums]] on May 22, 1998. The Democratic Unionist Party was the only major party in Northern Ireland to oppose it.

1990 American gangster film directed by [[Martin Scorsese]]. Adapted from Nicholas Pileggi's 1985 nonfiction book *Wiseguy*, it follows Mafia associate [[Henry Hill]] from 1955 to 1980, with [[Robert De Niro]], Ray Liotta and [[Joe Pesci]] in the leading roles. It premiered at the 47th Venice International Film Festival in September 1990. The film received six [[Academy Awards]] nominations, and Pesci won Best Supporting Actor. In 2000 the [[Library of Congress]] selected it for the National Film Registry as "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant."

American multinational technology corporation. Founded in 1998 by [[Larry Page]] and [[Sergey Brin]], Google went public in 2004, and in 2015 it became a wholly owned subsidiary of [[Alphabet Inc.]]. Its first product, [[Google Search]], was followed by services including [[Gmail]], [[YouTube]], [[Google Maps|Maps]], Chrome, Android and cloud storage. Google is the largest provider by market share of search engines, mapping and navigation applications, email, office suites, online video, mobile operating systems, web browsers, machine learning frameworks and AI virtual assistants. Google Search and YouTube are the two most-visited websites worldwide. Its operations include online advertising, [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]], quantum computing and self-driving cars through Waymo. Criticism has involved privacy concerns, tax avoidance, censorship, search neutrality, antitrust and abuse of its monopoly position.

Cross-platform [[Web browser|web browser]] developed by [[Google]]. Launched in September 2008 for Microsoft Windows, it was built with open-source components from WebKit and [[Firefox|Mozilla Firefox]], though most of its code comes from the Chromium project. It became the default browser on [[Android (operating system)|Android]] devices and is the main component of ChromeOS. As of October 2026, StatCounter estimated its worldwide share at 68.79% across all platforms, the most of any browser, and Chrome had approximately 3.62 billion users as of March 2026. Google later applied the "Chrome" name to other products, including Chromebook and Chromecast.

Web mapping platform and consumer application developed by [[Google]]. It offers satellite imagery, street maps, real-time traffic and route planning on foot, by car, by bike and by [[Public transport|public transportation]]. Google acquired the C++ desktop program, developed in [[Australia]], in October 2004, and launched it as a web application in February 2005. By 2013 its mobile app was the world's most popular [[Smartphone|smartphone]] app, used by over 54% of global smartphone owners. In 2018 the desktop version moved from a variant of the [[Mercator projection]] to a 3D globe. As of 2020 it was used by over one billion people every month.

[[Search engine]] operated by [[Google]]. Launched in 1998 as the company's first product, it was mostly developed by [[Larry Page]] and [[Sergey Brin]]. Users enter keywords into a search box, and results are indexed by PageRank and other proprietary [[Algorithm|algorithms]]. Since the 2020s it has been integrated with [[Generative AI|generative AI]] features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode. Google.com is the most-visited [[Website|website]] in the world, with an estimated 90% share of the global search-engine market as of 2026. In 2024 a U.S. federal court ruled in *United States v. Google LLC* that the company held an illegal [[Monopoly|monopoly]] over internet search and search advertising.

Waterfowl of several species in the family *Anatidae*, chiefly the [[Genus|genera]] *Anser* (grey geese and white geese) and *Branta* (black geese). [[Swan|Swans]] are generally larger than true geese, and [[Duck|ducks]] are smaller. "Goose" can refer to either sex, while "gander" denotes the male, and young birds before fledging are called goslings. Geese are monogamous and live in permanent pairs throughout the year, but are territorial only during the short nesting season. Most species are migratory, though [[Canada goose|Canada geese]] near human developments may stay year-round. [[Fossil|Fossils]] of true geese, dense in North America, date from about 10 million years ago in the [[Miocene]]. Goose-like birds are also known from subfossil remains on the [[Hawaiian Islands]].

Canadian [[Ice hockey|ice hockey]] player nicknamed "Mr. Hockey." He played 26 seasons in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL), 25 of them with the [[Detroit]] Red Wings, and six in the World Hockey Association. Born in [[Saskatchewan]] and raised in [[Saskatoon]], he held NHL records for 801 goals, 1,049 assists and 1,850 points at his retirement, and his record of 1,767 games played stood until 2021. He won four Stanley Cups with the Red Wings and six Hart Trophies as league MVP. In 1979–80, playing for the Hartford Whalers, he became the oldest person to play in an NHL game. The "Gordie Howe hat trick," a goal, an assist and a fight in one game, is named after him.

American psychologist. One of the first psychologists to study personality, he is considered a founder of [[Personality psychology]]. He rejected both psychoanalytic and behavioral approaches, which he judged too interpretive or too shallow, and developed an eclectic theory based on traits. He stressed each individual's uniqueness and the present context rather than history. Allport also explored topics such as rumor, [[Prejudice]] and [[Religion]]. He taught for a long career at [[Harvard University]], where his students included Jerome S. Bruner, Stanley Milgram and M. Brewster Smith. A 2002 survey ranked him the 11th most-cited psychologist of the 20th century.

Canadian singer-songwriter who helped define the singer-songwriter era of the 1970s. Born in Orillia, Ontario, he made his first appearance at Massey Hall in [[Toronto]] at age 12. His hits included "If You Could Read My Mind" (1970), "Sundown" (1974) and "The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald" (1976). His songs were widely covered, including "Ribbon of Darkness," a number one [[Country music|country]] hit for Marty Robbins. He performed at the opening ceremonies of the 1988 Winter Olympics. [[Bob Dylan]] said he could not think of a Lightfoot song he disliked.

British [[Celebrity|celebrity]] chef, restaurateur and television presenter. His restaurant group, founded in 1997, has been awarded 17 Michelin stars overall, and its flagship, Restaurant Gordon Ramsay in [[London]], has held three since 2001. His media persona, built on the 1999 documentary *Boiling Point* and series such as *Hell's Kitchen*, is defined by a fiery temper and frequent [[Profanity|profanity]]. Appointed an OBE by [[Elizabeth II]] in 2006 for services to the hospitality industry, he was listed by [[Forbes]] with 2020 earnings of US$70 million.

American writer and public intellectual known for his cynical, epigrammatic wit. His novel *The City and the Pillar* (1948) portrayed a male homosexual relationship dispassionately and offended conservative reviewers. His historical novel *Julian* (1964) recreated the world of the [[Roman emperor]] Julian the Apostate. His *Narratives of Empire* series, including *Burr* (1973) and *Lincoln* (1984), examined how public and private personality affect U.S. politics. He twice ran unsuccessfully as a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate, for the [[United States House of Representatives]] in 1960 and the [[United States Senate]] in 1982.

Genus of large, primarily herbivorous great apes of equatorial Africa. The genus has two species, the western and eastern gorillas, with four or five subspecies. Gorillas are the largest living [[Primate|primates]], reaching heights of up to 1.8 m and weights of up to 227 kg. Their [[DNA]] is highly similar to human DNA, from 96 to 99%, and after the [[Bonobo|bonobos]] and [[Chimpanzee|chimpanzees]] they are the next closest living relatives to humans. They live in troops led by a silverback, in forests of [[Sub-Saharan Africa]]. Both species are classified as Critically Endangered by the IUCN, and poaching, habitat destruction and disease threaten them. The word "gorilla" derives from accounts of [[Hanno the Navigator]], a Carthaginian explorer c. 500 BC who described hairy people on the West African coast, whom his interpreters called "Gorillae."

British virtual [[Alternative rock|alternative rock]] band formed in 1998 by Damon Albarn and Jamie Hewlett. Its four fictional members, 2-D, Murdoc Niccals, Noodle and Russel Hobbs, appear in music videos and comics, and Albarn is the only permanent musical contributor. Departing from the Britpop sound of [[Blur (band)|Blur]], Albarn explored [[Hip-hop|hip-hop]], electronic and world music. The self-titled 2001 debut album, *Gorillaz*, went triple platinum in the UK, and *Demon Days* (2005) spawned the single "Feel Good Inc." The band won a Grammy Award and Best British Group at the 2018 Brit Awards.

Korean dynasty (918–1392) that unified the Korean Peninsula after the Later Three Kingdoms period. Founded by the general Wang Kŏn, it gave its name to [[Korea]]. Buddhism was the state religion and reached its highest level of influence in Korean history, with 70 temples in the capital in the 11th century. Commerce flourished, with merchants arriving from as far as the [[Middle East]]. Goryeo fought the Liao and Jin, and was invaded by the [[Mongol Empire]], becoming a vassal of the [[Yuan dynasty]] in the 13th and 14th centuries. It later reclaimed territory as the Yuan declined. A proposed attack on the [[Ming dynasty]] led to a [[Coup d'état|coup]] by General Yi Sŏnggye, which ended the dynasty; [[Joseon]] followed in 1392.

Music-based subculture that emerged in the United Kingdom in the early 1980s from nightclubs and the [[Rock music|gothic rock]] genre. Its central venues included the F Club in [[Leeds]] and the Batcave in London's Soho, and by 1983 the NME had replaced the label "positive punk" with "goth." Dress usually includes dark, often solid black attire, dark makeup and black hair, drawing on Victorian and [[Belle Époque]] fashion as well as German Expressionism and classic [[Horror film|horror films]]. In the 1990s and 2000s it entered mainstream awareness, while the media often linked it to deviance and [[Self-harm|self-harm]]. It developed on early social networks such as [[Myspace|MySpace]].

City on Sweden's west coast (pop., c. 600,000), seat of Västra Götaland County. Sweden's second-largest city, after [[Stockholm]], lies on the [[Kattegat]] at the mouth of the Göta älv. King [[Gustavus Adolphus]] founded it by royal charter in 1621 as a fortified, primarily Dutch, trading colony during the [[Thirty Years' War]]. Its port is now the largest in the [[Nordic countries]]. Volvo was founded there in 1927 and remains headquartered in the city. The Gothia Cup, the world's largest youth football tournament, is held here.

Byzantine–Gothic war in Italy and nearby islands, 535–554. It was the last of the Gothic wars against the [[Byzantine Empire]], and it aimed to recover former Western Roman provinces lost to invading tribes during the [[Migration Period]], under [[Justinian I]]. The first phase saw Byzantine forces reconquer Italy under Belisarius, until the fall of Ravenna in 540. A Gothic revival under Totila was suppressed only after a long struggle by the Byzantine general Narses. In 554, Justinian's pragmatic sanction set Italy's new government, but the war devastated and depopulated the peninsula. It was a pyrrhic victory, as the [[Lombards]] invaded in 568 and [[Constantinople]] permanently lost large parts of Italy.

Architectural style prevalent in Europe from the late 12th to the 16th century. It evolved from [[Romanesque architecture]] and is characterized by pointed arches, rib vaults, flying buttresses and large, traceried stained-glass windows. It originated in the [[Île-de-France]] and Picardy regions of northern France, and the Abbey of Saint-Denis near [[Paris]] is considered the first Gothic building. [[Renaissance architecture|Renaissance architecture]] supplanted the style in Italy in the mid-15th century, but it flourished longer in England and what is now Belgium. Though especially associated with churches, it was also used for [[Castle|castles]], palaces, town halls, universities and houses. The term "Gothic" was first applied contemptuously during the later Renaissance, and [[Giorgio Vasari]] attributed its features to the [[Goths]].
